description: Notes from the human editor directing the curmudgeon to review specific items with specific focus areas. Check at the start of every run. Pending notes take priority over the normal tracker sequence. Mark notes as consumed after reviewing.

notes.topic: Review the ISS-3113 Chapman-1933 cross-surface patch set (30 exact-text patches) before integration
notes.context: Do this AFTER HNOTE-OPERATOR-ECLIPSE-MAGNETIC-REV5-CYCLE5-2026-10-16 if that is still pending (older first; one per run). The analyst (2026-10-18, cloud mode) proposes 30 exact-text patches across sections.json (parts 1, 1b, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10), KS-005 x4 and the PRED-095 tldr/detail. They re-describe Chapman 1933 as the first theoretical treatment, whose author judged that the data of the time did not show the effect. notes.mechanism: Single operator-commission review, class deep-attack on citations and wording, narrow scope. Write reviews/ISS-3113-chapman-cross-surface.c1.json with per-patch accept/fix/reject and a recommendation.
review_focus_hints: Verify Chapman 1933 (doi 10.1029/TE038i003p00175) and Kim & Chang 2018 (doi 10.1016/j.asr.2018.01.022) directly. Check that each patch says no more than the source does. This cluster has had four citation failures.

Check that removing the 5-25 nT range does not leave any sentence without a quantitative claim it still needs. The analyst points to the sourced baseline-rescaling argument in 4.2.5; check it actually supports each place it replaces.
Confirm the 4.2.6 pre-commitment is annotated, not rewritten. Rewriting a pre-commitment after the event is goalpost-moving.

Out-of-scope items the analyst flagged (WIN-025 '5-30 nT' and 'known since Chapman (1919)'; WIN-068 '39 eclipses' attributed to Kim & Chang 2018): say whether they should be filed as a follow-up issue.
